implementation_notes: The conventional C++ instance: + is the combine, a static identity() (or default constructor) is the empty, and std::accumulate is the fold. Works with the standard algorithms unchanged.
idiom_name: operator+ overload with a static identity()
pitfalls: Non-trivial default construction as the identity is a hidden cost in every fold.

variants.name: Free combine function plus explicit identity
variants.idiom_name: namespace-scope combine(a, b) / identity() free functions
variants.implementation_notes: A lighter option that avoids the pre-C++20 restriction on friend operator+ and keeps the algebra as named free functions, which reads well when the instance also has to satisfy concepts or be passed to a generic fold.
variants.code_sketch:
namespace monoid { Money identity(); Money combine(Money, Money); }
template <class M> M fold(std::vector<M> xs, M (*op)(M, M), M (*id)());
pitfalls: Free functions in a namespace must be found by ADL or an explicit qualification; a missed qualification is a compile error, not a silent default.
